name: linear-synthetic
description: Linear bandit: 10 instances (1000 actions and theta uniform on the unit sphere of R^20, noise 0.1), 2 runs each. LinUCB and ConfidenceBall1 against arm buckets (LinUCB_AB), random projections (LinUCB_RP, CBRAP), sketches (SOFUL, CBSCFD) and LinTS. Theoretical defaults.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: Values of the papers: LinUCB alpha=1, ConfidenceBall1 alpha=1, LinUCB_AB alpha=1, LinUCB_RP alpha=1, CBRAP alpha=1, SOFUL alpha=1, CBSCFD alpha=1, LinTS alpha=1. They give the theoretical confidence bounds: safe in theory, but they often explore too much in practice. To fit them to this problem, run a grid search (param_grid=True, or "param_grid": true in a config file) or set them, e.g. LinUCB(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Arm buckets (heuristic)
notices.text: LinUCB_AB sorts the actions by estimated mean and cuts them into n_buckets buckets, rebuilt after bucket_rebuild_freq updates. A step compares the best action of each bucket, then searches the chosen bucket only. This is faster on many actions, but it can miss the action the policy without buckets would play, and the regret bound of its paper no longer holds.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret (track "pseudo_regret"); n_buckets, sketch_error over time (track "clusters"); action of every step (track "actions"); peak memory (measure_memory=True). The dashboard and the figures cannot show what is not stored; the brackets say how to store it (in a config file: "track": [...] or "measure_memory": true in "experiment").

notices.title: One point every 15 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 15 steps and the last step (log_interval=15). The values at these points are exact. Between two points, the charts draw a straight line: there the curve is interpolated, not measured. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: With n_jobs=4, each process uses one BLAS thread: compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
